experiment: ordered latest-series map in the fused Mimir instant scan
retention_decision: Reject: median total CPU rises 6.8% and query p99 rises 9.8%. Both are higher in every matched pair, with disjoint ranges. Querier CPU rises in all three pairs, also with disjoint ranges. Peak RSS is mixed and its median rises 1.3%. Ingestion is mixed. Preserve the verified diagnostics, three-pair control and native comparison; remove the ordered-map production change and retain the complete sample/label ledger.

scope.change: Use BTreeMap for the latest-series map and consume it in fingerprint order. Remove the temporary vector and final sort. Preserve the separate cold conflict map, matcher identity checks, one hot snapshot, cold precedence, duplicate ties, stale markers, limits and all fallback paths.

profile_selection.interpretation: Unchanged production scan bytes connect the prior GCP profile to this baseline. Sample shares identify a hypothesis; they do not establish a gain.

negative_control.result: Exactly the full production scan ledger fails; 65 other metrics-service tests pass. Candidate source restored afterward.

comparison_plan: Two independently checksummed release images on one private GCP VM. Three fresh alternating baseline/candidate pairs, plus three native Mimir pairs. Steady load 60 seconds, matched aggregate budgets, accepted rows, query completions, scrape coverage and OOM gates. CPU and peak RSS include broker and MinIO.
measurement_limitations: Single-node API-accepted workload; native durability/publication contracts differ.
No timing or resource advantage claimed before the uninstrumented control completes.
